title: WPMS/2715/2014 of M/s Score Information Technologies Ltd AND ANOTHER Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND ANOTHER

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (M/S) No.2715 of 2014

M/s Score Information Tech. Ltd. & another
 ....Petitioners
Versus
State & another ....Respondents
Mr. Arvind Vashisth, Sr. Advocate assisted by Mr. Lalit Sharma, Advocate for the petitioners.
Mr. S.N. Babulkar, Advocate General assisted by Mr. Paresh Tripathi, C.S.C., for the State of
Uttarakhand/respondent no.1.
Mr. Shobhit Saharia, Advocate, for the High Court/respondent no.2.
Dated- 13.09.2017
Hon'ble Rajiv Sharma, J
 Respondent no.2 invited tenders by way of Two-Bid System for Supply, Installation, Commissioning,
Operation and Maintenance of IP Based CCTV Surveillance
System for the purpose of Security, Monitoring and
Recording within the High Court Premises at Nainital as
well as in the Complexes of Courts Subordinate to the High
Court of Uttarakhand. The last date of receipt of Bid
submission was 14.9.2012 at 3:30 PM. The date of opening
of Technical Bid documents was 14.9.2012. Date of
theoretical evaluation was 17.9.2012 which was
subsequently changed to 29.9.2012. The earnest money
deposit was Rs.2.00 lakh which was subsequently
enhanced to Rs.5.00 lakh.
2. Petitioner participated in the tendering process.
The financial bid was open. He was the L-1. The High
Court has entered into a negotiation with the petitioner
whereby the amount was reduced to Rs.41 crores from
Rs.44 crores. However, in the meantime, a letter was
received from the State Government on 19.8.2014, on the
basis of which, a conscious decision was taken by the High
Court on 16/17.09.2014 cancelling the process of
procurement, installation and maintenance of CCTV

2
Surveillance System. The Earnest Money Deposit (EMD)
made by the petitioner was ordered to be returned.
3. The EMD was returned to the petitioner vide
communication dated 16.9.2014. The Bank Guarantee of
Rs.5.00 lakh was also remitted back on 18.9.2014.
4. The fact of the matter is that the decision was
taken by the High Court on 16/17.9.2014 on the basis of
communication dated 19.8.2014 addressed to it by the
State Government, as per the contents of counter affidavit,
more particularly in Paragraph No.66.
5. Petitioners have not specifically assailed the
order dated 19.08.2014, on the basis of which, the
communication dated 16/17.09.2014 was issued by the
Registrar of this Court.
6. It is settled law that the petitioners are required
to place on record the letter/notification etc., which they
wished to assail by way of writ petition. It is the prerogative
of the Employer either to go ahead or not to go ahead with
the process of culmination of NIT beyond the financial bid.
The scope of judicial review in these matters is very limited.
The Court would like to put a caveat that in those cases,
where there is arbitrariness, discrimination is writ large in
the matters pertaining to tenders, the Court can only look
into the decision making process and not the merits of the
matter, as per the law laid down by the Hon. Apex Court in
the case of Tata Cellular vs. Union of India (1994) 6 SCC
Page 651.
7. It would be apt to mention at this stage that Mr.
Shobhit Saharia, learned Counsel appearing for the High
Court, has submitted at the Bar that though the
Procurement Rules of 2008, per se, cannot be binding upon

3
the High Court but these are followed by the High Court in
letter and spirit in order to maintain the transparency.
8. By accepting the E.M.D. and subsequently the
Bank Guarantee, petitioner has acquiesced/waived his
rights. In view of this, the petitioner is estopped from filing
the writ petition.
9. In view of the observation and discussion, made
hereinabove, there is no merit in this petition and the same
is hereby dismissed.
10. Interim application, if any, stands disposed of.
 (Rajiv Sharma, J.)
Rdang
